name: Example: Finding the Lower Triangular Matrix Given the Elementary Row Operations
problem:
Suppose that a $3 \times 3$ matrix $F$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
R_2:=R_2+R_1, \qquad
	R_3:=R_3+2R_1
$$

Given that $F$ has the LU factorization $F=LU,$ then $L=$
worked_solution:
Applying $R_2:=R_2 + {\color{red}1} \cdot R_1$ and then $R_3:=R_3+ {\color{red}2} \cdot R_1$ is equivalent to multiplying $F$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062432/assets/5eb696ca679a0079e8460d472b6f172df4f2e29f5dfef6cbdee388c55dcb1db5.png)

Now, since $E_2E_1F=U,$ we can invert $E_2$ and $E_1$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}F & =U \\ {E}_{1}F & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ F & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ F & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ F & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ F & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$
